paper_title: Improved asthma control with budesonide/formoterol in a single inhaler, compared with budesonide alone
design_rationale: The study explicitly reports computerized random allocation to three parallel treatment groups, with treatment codes retained in sealed envelopes.

domain_judgments.rationale: The allocation sequence was computerized by country, treatment codes were kept sealed until data analysis, and reported baseline characteristics were comparable across groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Computerized randomization occurred on a per-country basis and individual treatment codes were kept in sealed envelopes until data analysis.

domain_judgments.rationale: Double-blind, double-dummy procedures minimized awareness of assignment, adherence was similarly high across groups, and efficacy analyses included all randomized participants under a stated intention-to-treat approach.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: All efficacy variables were analysed on an intention-to-treat basis, using data from all patients who had taken ≥1 dose of study medication.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although all 362 randomized patients were included in analyses and discontinuation numbers and reasons were balanced, 53 participants (14.6%) discontinued and the handling or completeness of their subsequent diary outcome data is not described.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A total of 53 patients (20 single inhaler therapy; 17 separate inhaler therapy; 16 budesonide alone) discontinued the study.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary PEF outcome was measured identically in all groups using a specified peak-flow meter and standardized procedures, while double-blind double-dummy treatment reduced the potential for participant knowledge to influence measurement.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: PEF was measured using a mini-Wright® peak flow meter (Clement Clark, Harlow, UK) before intake of study medication, and the highest of three values was recorded.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome and primary comparison were prespecified in the article, but no prospective registration or accessible statistical analysis plan is reported, and numerous secondary outcomes plus explicitly post hoc time-period analyses leave some scope for selective reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: This trend in favour of the single inhaler therapy versus separate inhaler therapy approached significance for morning PEF (primary variable) during weeks 2 and 3 (p<0.07, post hoc analysis).

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is judged as some concerns. Randomization, blinding, intervention adherence, analysis population, and standardized outcome measurement were generally strong, but attrition of about 15% was not accompanied by clear reporting of missing-data handling, and the absence of registration or an available analysis plan leaves some risk of selective reporting.

paper_title: Can guideline-defined asthma control be achieved? The Gaining Optimal Asthma ControL study
design_rationale: The abstract explicitly describes the study as a “randomized, stratified, double-blind, parallel-group study” comparing two treatment strategies.

domain_judgments.rationale: Random assignment is explicitly stated, but the abstract does not describe sequence generation, allocation concealment, or baseline balance, so the integrity of the randomization process cannot be fully verified.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A 1-year, randomized, stratified, double-blind, parallel-group study of 3,421 patients with uncontrolled asthma compared fluticasone propionate and salmeterol/fluticasone

domain_judgments.rationale: Double blinding reduces concern about deviations related to treatment awareness, and protocolized dose escalation is described, but adherence, unintended deviations, and the analysis population or intention-to-treat approach are not reported in the abstract.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Treatment was stepped-up until total control was achieved (or maximum 500 microg corticosteroid twice a day).

domain_judgments.rationale: The abstract reports outcomes using group counts but does not state attrition, completeness of outcome data, or how missing observations were handled over the one-year follow-up.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Total control was achieved across all strata: 520 (31%) versus 326 (19%) patients after dose escalation (p < 0.001) and 690 (41%) versus 468 (28%) at 1 year

domain_judgments.rationale: Asthma control was assessed using prespecified composite guideline-based measures, and double blinding makes differential outcome assessment between treatment groups unlikely.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: compared fluticasone propionate and salmeterol/fluticasone in achieving two rigorous, composite, guideline-based measures of control: totally and well-controlled asthma

domain_judgments.rationale: Multiple outcomes and time points are reported, but the abstract provides no protocol, registration, or prespecified statistical analysis plan with which to exclude selective choice among eligible measurements or analyses.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Total control was achieved across all strata: 520 (31%) versus 326 (19%) patients after dose escalation (p < 0.001) and 690 (41%) versus 468 (28%) at 1 year

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is judged as some concerns. Although this was a randomized, double-blind trial with guideline-based outcome measures, the available abstract does not adequately report allocation concealment, baseline balance, missing-data handling, analysis population, or safeguards against selective reporting.

paper_title: Long-term treatment with fluticasone propionate/salmeterol via Diskus improves asthma control versus fluticasone propionate alone
design_rationale: The available text states that subjects received one of two treatments but does not explicitly describe random sequence generation or any other random allocation mechanism, so the study must be classified as non-randomized under the specified rule.

domain_judgments.rationale: Because allocation was not reported as random and no baseline comparability or confounder-adjusted analysis was described, differences in asthma severity or other prognostic factors could plausibly account for part of the observed treatment effect.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Three hundred six subjects received FSC 250/50 micrograms and 315 subjects received FP 250 micrograms.

domain_judgments.domain_name: Bias due to selection of participants into the study
domain_judgments.rationale: Eligibility was limited to subjects symptomatic during open-label FP 100 micrograms treatment, but the timing and mechanism of selection into the comparison groups were not reported, leaving plausible selection bias.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: This 52-week study was designed to assess the safety and efficacy of fluticasone propionate/salmeterol combination (FSC) 250/50 micrograms versus fluticasone propionate (FP) 250 micrograms in subjects with persistent asthma symptomatic on open-label FP 100 micrograms.

domain_judgments.rationale: The two pharmacologic regimens, doses, delivery context, and twice-daily schedule were clearly distinguished, making intervention misclassification unlikely.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Three hundred six subjects received FSC 250/50 micrograms and 315 subjects received FP 250 micrograms. Both treatments were administered twice daily.

domain_judgments.domain_name: Bias due to deviations from intended interventions
domain_judgments.rationale: The abstract does not report blinding, adherence, treatment switching, co-interventions, or whether analyses retained participants in their initially assigned groups, so intervention-related deviations cannot be excluded.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Both treatments were administered twice daily.

domain_judgments.rationale: No information is provided on attrition, completeness of 52-week outcome data, or methods used to address missing observations.

FEV1 is an appropriate objective pulmonary-function outcome and attack criteria were defined, but the abstract does not report assessor blinding or whether knowledge of treatment could influence effort-dependent spirometry and symptom, albuterol-use, or urgent-care outcomes.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary objective of this study was to show that FSC 250/50 micrograms was superior to FP 250 micrograms at increasing pulmonary function as measured by forced expiratory volume in 1 second over a 52-week treatment period.

domain_judgments.domain_name: Bias in selection of the reported result
domain_judgments.rationale: No protocol or preregistration is reported, and several efficacy outcomes and asthma-attack definitions were available, creating scope for selective choice of analyses or reported results.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A secondary objective was to compare the rate of asthma attacks defined as (1) a sustained 2-day decrease in morning peak expiratory flow or increase in albuterol use for 2 consecutive days, (2) an asthma exacerbation requiring systemic corticosteroids, or (3) an unscheduled clinic or hospital visit for acute asthma symptoms.

overall_summary: Overall ROBINS-I risk is serious, driven principally by serious potential confounding because random allocation, baseline comparability, and adjustment were not reported. Missing-data information was absent, and incomplete reporting of deviations, blinding, and prespecification added further uncertainty.

paper_title: Efficacy and safety of fluticasone/formoterol combination therapy in patients with moderate-to-severe asthma
design_rationale: The study explicitly reports random allocation using minimisation with biased-coin assignment, implemented through an Interactive Voice Response System.

domain_judgments.rationale: The allocation method was explicitly randomized, balanced on prespecified prognostic factors, centrally implemented, and produced broadly comparable baseline groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Patients were randomised according to minimisation with biased coin assignment... An Interactive Voice Response System was used for subject enrolment and treatment allocation.

domain_judgments.rationale: Double-dummy blinding and monitoring of adherence reduced concern about intervention deviations, but the efficacy analysis excluded randomized participants without specified post-baseline measurements rather than clearly using intention-to-treat analysis.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The efficacy analyses were carried out on the full analysis set (FAS), which included all randomised patients who had at least one dose of study medication, a pre-dose FEV1 measurement at baseline, a pre-dose FEV1 measurement post-baseline, and a 2-h post-dose FEV1 measurement postbaseline.

domain_judgments.rationale: Only 70.9% completed the trial, discontinuation was strongly differential and often related to lack of efficacy, and LOCF is unlikely to remove bias from such informative missingness.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: In total, 395 (70.9%) patients completed the study and 162 (29.1%) discontinued... Missing observed data for both the primary and secondary efficacy analyses were managed using last observation carried forward (LOCF) imputation.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary spirometric outcomes were objective and measured at common scheduled visits, while extensive double-dummy blinding made differential assessment unlikely.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: All investigators, personnel at the study site, and representatives involved in monitoring, data management and any other aspect of the trial, including sponsor personnel, were blinded throughout the study.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was registered and the co-primary endpoints and gatekeeping strategy were described, but no protocol or prespecified statistical analysis plan was available here to verify that reported measurements and analyses were selected as planned.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: This was a 12-week, randomised, double-blind, placeboand active-controlled, stratified, parallel-group study... EudraCT number: 2006-005989-39; US NCT number: NCT00393952.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is high because nearly 30% of randomized participants discontinued, attrition was differential and frequently related to efficacy, and LOCF cannot reliably address informative missingness. Additional concerns arise from the modified analysis population and inability to verify outcome-selection decisions against a protocol or analysis plan.

paper_title: Once-daily fluticasone furoate/vilanterol reduces risk of severe exacerbations in asthma versus fluticasone furoate alone
design_rationale: This was an explicitly randomized parallel-group trial; allocation used an automated telephone system and a computer-generated schedule.

domain_judgments.rationale: The sequence was computer-generated and implemented through an automated telephone system, and measured baseline characteristics were generally balanced, but the report does not explicitly state that the system concealed allocation from enrolling personnel until assignment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Patients were randomised using an automated interactive telephone-based system (RAMOS; GlaxoSmithKline, UK) in accordance with a computer-generated schedule (RandAll; GlaxoSmithKline, UK).

domain_judgments.rationale: The study was double-blind, treatments used the same inhaler schedule, and the primary efficacy analysis used the ITT population, with no evidence that deviations related to trial context biased the effect estimate.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: All efficacy and safety analyses were carried out in the intent-to-treat (ITT) population other than those specified as being carried out in the per protocol (PP) population.

domain_judgments.rationale: The ITT analysis included 2019 of 2020 randomized participants, treatment exposure was similar between groups, and sensitivity analyses found no evidence of differential informative censoring.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The possibility of informative censoring was explored. The Kaplan–Meier curves for time to first severe asthma exacerbation or withdrawal due to lack of efficacy, investigator discretion or withdrawal of consent between the two treatment groups did not differ from those of the primary analysis.

domain_judgments.rationale: Severe exacerbations were defined using standardized ERS/ATS criteria and reviewed by a blinded independent adjudication committee consistently across groups, making differential outcome measurement unlikely.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A blinded independent adjudication committee ensured that all severe asthma exacerbations were captured as defined in the protocol.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered and the primary endpoint and model are clearly specified, but the supplied report does not provide the protocol or statistical analysis plan needed to exclude selective choice among analyses, and an interim analysis introduced additional analytic flexibility.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: One interim analysis was performed to evaluate the primary endpoint (ie, time to first severe asthma exacerbation) and to identify any potential treatment harm.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is some concerns, driven by incomplete explicit reporting of allocation concealment and insufficient information from the protocol/statistical analysis plan to fully exclude selective reporting. Blinding, ITT analysis, near-complete inclusion, censoring sensitivity analyses, and blinded adjudication otherwise support low risk.

paper_title: Budesonide/formoterol fumarate dihydrate versus budesonide with a novel suspension technology for uncontrolled asthma: phase 3 LITHOS study
design_rationale: This was explicitly described as a randomized, double-blind, parallel-group trial, with participants assigned 1:1 through a centralized interactive response technology system.

domain_judgments.rationale: Centralized 1:1 allocation through an interactive response technology system was concealed by kit identification numbers, and baseline characteristics were generally balanced, with no compelling evidence of randomization failure.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Participant randomisation was performed using an interactive response technology (IRT) system. The IRT system provided the study investigators or pharmacists with a kit identification number to be allocated to the participant at the dispensing visit in order to maintain the blinding between BFF MDI and BD MDI.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants, care providers, investigators, and outcome assessors were blinded and adherence was monitored, but 21 randomized participants were not included in the treated efficacy set and the analysis was therefore not a full intention-to-treat analysis; exclusions related to site GCP violations are insufficiently detailed.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Efficacy analyses were conducted in the efficacy set (all randomised participants who received any treatment).

domain_judgments.rationale: Week-12 primary outcome data were available for 343 of 353 treated participants (97.2%), discontinuation was limited, and the small amount of missingness was unlikely to materially bias the effect estimate.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Of a total 374 randomised participants, 353 were treated (BFF_A 160, n=179; BD 160, n=174) and 341 completed the study (BFF_A 160, n=176; BD 160, n=165).

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome, spirometric FEV1 AUC0–3, was objective and measured consistently across groups, while outcome assessors were blinded, making differential measurement unlikely.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The participant, care provider, investigator and outcomes assessor were blinded during the study.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered, the primary and key secondary outcomes and multiplicity procedures were prespecified for the regional approaches, and post hoc or unadjusted analyses were explicitly identified.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: This clinical trial is prospectively registered with ClinicalTrials.gov as NCT05755906.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is judged some concerns, driven by use of a treated efficacy set rather than a full intention-to-treat population and insufficient detail about the randomized participants excluded following site GCP violations. Randomization, outcome completeness among treated participants, blinded objective outcome measurement, and prospective outcome specification otherwise support low risk.

paper_title: Budesonide/formoterol fumarate dihydrate versus budesonide with a novel suspension technology for uncontrolled asthma: phase 3 VATHOS study
design_rationale: The supplied text explicitly describes randomized allocation in both clinical trials, including Trial 1 randomized 1:1:1:1 and Trial 2 randomized 2:2:1:1, although it appears to be a BREZTRI COPD prescribing label rather than the titled VATHOS asthma report.

domain_judgments.rationale: Random assignment and allocation ratios are stated, but the sequence-generation method, allocation concealment, and treatment-specific baseline balance are not reported in the supplied text.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Trial 1 (NCT02465567) was conducted over 52 weeks in a total of 8,588 subjects randomized (1:1:1:1)

domain_judgments.rationale: Although the trials were largely double-blind, Trial 2 included an open-label comparator and the efficacy analyses excluded observations after treatment discontinuation rather than clearly using an intention-to-treat strategy, creating potential bias from intervention-related deviations and censoring.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The analysis excluded spirometry data collected after discontinuation of study treatment.

domain_judgments.rationale: The label does not report the extent or reasons for missing outcome data, and its on-treatment analyses excluded post-discontinuation outcomes, so results could be biased if discontinuation differed by treatment or prognosis.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: On-treatment analyses excluded exacerbation data collected after discontinuation of study treatment.

domain_judgments.rationale: The main outcomes were defined and measured consistently using objective spirometry or prespecified clinical criteria, and the principal treatment comparisons were conducted in double-blind trials.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The clinical efficacy of BREZTRI AEROSPHERE has been evaluated in two (Trial 1 and 2) randomized, double-blind, multicenter, parallel-group trials

domain_judgments.rationale: Trial registrations and primary endpoints are identified, but the supplied label provides no protocol or statistical analysis plan sufficient to verify that reported outcome measurements and analyses were prespecified, and it presents several endpoints and subgroup analyses.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: In Trial 2, the primary endpoints were FEV1 area under the curve from 0-4 hours ... and change from baseline in morning pre-dose trough FEV1 at Week 24

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is high because efficacy analyses excluded data after treatment discontinuation without adequate reporting of missingness, potentially biasing estimated treatment effects. There are additional concerns about incompletely reported randomization/concealment and selective reporting, and the supplied document does not match the titled VATHOS asthma study.

paper_title: Pharmacogenetic studies of long-acting beta agonist and inhaled corticosteroid responsiveness in randomised controlled trials of individuals of African descent with asthma
design_rationale: The parent BARD trials explicitly randomized 574 participants to four step-up treatment combinations in a crossover design, and this paper is a secondary pharmacogenetic analysis of those randomized trials.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although allocation is explicitly described as randomized, the report does not describe sequence generation or allocation concealment and does not provide treatment-arm baseline comparisons for the pharmacogenetic analysis sample.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The BARD trials randomized 574 individuals with asthma uncontrolled with low-dose ICS ... to four different step-up combinations therapies.

domain_judgments.rationale: The crossover trial monitored medication access and compliance, but blinding and analysis according to randomized assignment are not clearly reported here, so effects of awareness or deviations cannot be excluded.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Factors not considered in this power estimate include the BARD cross-over trial design that monitored access and compliance to different controller therapies in the same individuals.

domain_judgments.rationale: Only 516 of the 574 randomized participants were included in the genotyped pharmacogenetic analyses, and the report does not explain exclusions or establish that missing genotype/outcome data were unrelated to treatment response.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: We performed ancestry-based pharmacogenetic studies ... in 249 unrelated children and 267 unrelated adults and adolescents genotyped with the Illumina Multi-Ethnic Global Array (MEGA) genotyping array.

domain_judgments.rationale: The prespecified hierarchical composite outcome used clinically relevant and consistently defined exacerbation, asthma-control-day, and lung-function components within the crossover trial, with no clear indication of differential ascertainment by treatment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: We performed ancestry-based pharmacogenetic studies of the BARD primary hierarchal composite outcome of pairwise superior responsiveness based on asthma exacerbations, a 31-day difference in annualized asthma-control days, or a five percent difference in percentage predicted FEV.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trials were registered and the analysis used stated co-primary comparisons and genome-wide thresholds, but the paper reports numerous treatment comparisons, age-stratified analyses, fine-mapping models, and secondary outcomes without a clearly cited prospective pharmacogenetic analysis plan, leaving scope for selective reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: For admixture mapping, we stratified by children and the pooled adolescent and adult groups and designated the step up to 5xICS versus 2–2.5xICS and 5xICS versus FP100SAL as our primary pairwise comparisons without adjustment for the multiple treatment arm comparisons similar to the parent study.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is judged some concerns. The study arose from randomized crossover trials and used an appropriate primary composite outcome, but sequence concealment, blinding/assignment-based analysis, reasons for excluding randomized participants, and prospective specification of the extensive pharmacogenetic analyses were insufficiently reported.
